question: Why does Ibn Turka raise the written form of the letter above the spoken?
proposition: His preference for the written form expresses a millenarian consciousness: the conviction of living at a new phase of human evolution that can gather all accumulated knowledge.
reasoning: Melvin-Koushki calls the lionization of the written form a quintessential expression of Ibn Turka's millenarian consciousness (pdf p.350).
Ibn Turka's own stated reasons are different in kind: writing endures and carries the full complexity of prophecy; light-borne letterforms do not clash (pdf pp.355-356).
The two are compatible; only the first is a reading of motive.
